PROGRESS ISN’T A STRAIGHT LINE.

A GOAL TO CHASE.
ROOM TO REASSESS.

Stride separates a faster ambition from an uncertain future scenario. It recognises when recent results have flattened or slowed. Its planning rules aren’t validated predictions, and they can’t tell you your lifetime limit.

Use the checkpoints, notice how you’re recovering, and make the plan fit the runner you are today.

BEFORE YOU LACE UP

A FEW
GOOD QUESTIONS.

Do I need a long running history?

No. Start with one result and add more when you have them. A trend assessment needs at least three comparable same-distance results spanning 60 days. With less evidence, Stride makes the uncertainty clear.

Can I choose my own target?

Yes. Edit your race goal finish time, or set today’s run by pace, distance or total time. Changes to your daily energy check-in won’t silently overwrite a custom pace.

Is my running information uploaded?

Your race inputs are processed in the browser. Choose “Save my history” to keep them on that device. There is no account or cross-device sync. Location is requested only when starting a GPS run; coordinates are not uploaded or saved.

Can I use it on my Garmin watch?

This release is a phone web app with a watch-inspired run screen. It isn’t a native Garmin app. Keep the page open and the phone unlocked for live use; outdoor GPS and device-specific behaviour still need field testing.

Does Stride guarantee a personal best?

No. Targets and timelines are planning suggestions, not promises or medical advice. Recovery, training consistency, conditions and your individual response all matter. Repeat or reduce a week when needed.

NO ACCOUNT. JUST A STARTING LINE.
